stances_toward.note: Our reading, confidence C: no source in this pass uses the word. The grade rests on structure: the Polisario claims a state on the territory Rabat calls its own, rejects any process that predetermines autonomy, and has been in armed conflict with Morocco since the ceasefire collapsed in Nov 2020 (date from the Wikipedia infobox of the 2020 clashes; no citation retrieved), with Algeria backing it. Rabat denies the Sahrawi Republic's existence as a state. Against 'adversary': the Polisario sat at the US-convened talks of Feb 2026, so the next pass should test 'rival'. Bond - grievance: an open dispute over the territory.

relations_to.summary: Rabat denies that the Polisario speaks for a Sahrawi state and rejects a process that keeps independence open: the Polisario, backed by Algeria, insists that any self-determination process include every option under international law; Bourita said in Dec 2025 that self-determination can take different forms within the autonomy plan and is not synonymous with a referendum.

relations_to.summary: US-convened negotiating rounds on implementing Resolution 2797: Madrid (early Feb 2026) and Washington (23-24 Feb 2026), with Bourita for Morocco, Attaf for Algeria, a Mauritanian representative and a Polisario delegate, Massad Boulos and Michael Waltz for the US and Staffan de Mistura for the UN; Rabat is to table a detailed dossier on its plan. No settlement was reached.
